annotation.title_clean: UN Regulation No 171 – Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regard to Driver Control Assistance Systems (DCAS)
annotation.title_en: UN Regulation No 171 – Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regard to Driver Control Assistance Systems (DCAS)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UN/ECE), published in the Official Journal of the European Union
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union (2024/2689)
annotation.summary_en: UN Regulation No 171 sets uniform type-approval requirements for SAE Level 2 Driver Control Assistance Systems in M and N category vehicles. It requires driver monitoring, warning escalation, system boundary handling, controllability, in-service monitoring and incident reporting, audits, physical and virtual validation, and software identification. The driver remains responsible for vehicle control.
key_provisions_or_claims: Type approval of DCAS (SAE L2) for M and N vehicles; driver remains responsible for control.
Driver monitoring of hands and eyes with escalating warnings, ending in a risk mitigation stop.
Rules for lane changes and other manoeuvres, speed limits, controllability and failure responses.
Manufacturers must report safety-critical occurrences and give yearly in-service data to the approval authority.
Validation by safety-management audit, track and road tests, and credibility-assessed virtual testing; software identification via RXSWIN and UN R156 compliance.
